ideas.text: Cache Keeper mod: reserve = measured cost per ping x pings needed until reset, with the user's tier table as the minimum.
Two-threshold safe stop: wrap-up line with a Status.md handoff note, then a hard floor that holds new prompts and edits.
Status line, band above the prompt, /cache on/off/status/reserve commands, a ping log pane, dry run and a toast on reset.
A Cache Keeper side pane with a usage timeline, reset countdown and full ping log.
Warnings when the weekly (7-day) window, not the 5h window, is the real limit.
A 'keep hot until' option for a set time instead of only an idle-hours cap.
Video and photo editing tools inside the hub, prototyped as local browser tools like Motion Studio.
Request form for other departments to fix late-information intake, the Director's named biggest blocker.
Consent and media-rights register with face blurring and metadata removal for beneficiary photos.
Toggle between Direction A and new identity by double-clicking the sidebar logo, persisted per browser.
Serve new identity fonts locally behind a single root-element switch after 0.3.1.1 token clean-up.
Evening (dark) mode for the new identity, with its own contrast table (task 0.3.4.3).
A QA component page showing every component state in both designs (task 0.3.2.3).
Aref Ruqaa accent word per page and IBM Plex Mono, installed once a screen uses them.
Add a phone and keyboard path for switching designs, since the logo double-click is desktop-only.
Show an «عاجل» mark in the prototype if the owner wants the Director to see it at the re-check.
Show the editor's name on each version («حرره محمد») in the prototype.
Command palette (Ctrl K) for the new design, only if the Director wants it.
Persist calendar move requests in the shared store so navigation does not drop them.
Make the phone approval sheet sit above the bottom bar before the user scrolls.
Keep prototype data in the browser across refresh, with a «إعادة ضبط السيناريو» reset button.
Single npm run qa command running all browser suites and tests together.
Draft the Version 1 Checkpoint 1.1 plan (Vercel and Supabase setup) for approval once the gate closes.
Add a change-password screen for signed-in users; today only the forgot-password email flow exists.
Move work items and approvals into Supabase so permissions are enforced on shared data.
Run the older QA scripts with a signed-in session once the owner has set passwords.
Start admin accounts as the director role instead of Admin, if the owner prefers.
Block a reviewer from approving a work they submitted themselves.
Offer to mark the owner's email confirmed from the database so first sign-in does not depend on email delivery.
Configure custom SMTP in Supabase to avoid the built-in mail rate limit.
Connect a Google Shared Drive or SharePoint library through a service account, with browser-direct resumable uploads.
Keep thumbnails and previews in Supabase Storage so the media grid stays fast.
Add per-campaign subfolders and attach uploaded files to work items and approvals in place of the mock assets.
Add an in-app password change screen and an audit log of sign-ins and uploads.
Move to Google Workspace with a Shared Drive and service account behind the same adapter.
Move to a Google Workspace Shared Drive with a service account when the organisation upgrades.
Store small preview thumbnails in Supabase Storage so the media grid loads fast.
Add a password-change screen inside the app.
Use the new brand logo PNGs as favicon and app icon in the Hub itself
Add the logo to the Google consent screen once brand verification is acceptable
Use the 512px rosette logo as favicon and app icon once the owner approves it.
Add a visible warning in the Hub when the Drive refresh token is near expiry or revoked.
Submit the app for Google verification later so the logo shows on the consent screen.
Use the brand SVG as the site favicon and app icon from public/brand.
Move to a custom domain so Google authorised-domain and verification steps are simpler and the logo can be added later.
Create Hub folders from campaigns and work items, and rename or move them in Drive from the website.
Per-folder access rules by person or role (view, edit, manage, hidden), enforced in the database.
Lock approved asset versions, and show real Drive storage figures in Admin Storage.
Auto-create a Drive folder per campaign and per work item, and attach uploads to the work item
Time-limited review links for outside reviewers, with open tracking in the activity feed
Thumbnails and real Drive storage figures in Admin, plus a per-folder audit trail
Implement real folders, rename, move and per-folder access rules on Drive and Supabase, with a logged action trail.
Add a pipeline-stage field, tasks table and quick-action permissions per role to the real database.
Time-limited review links for people without accounts.
Share-link signed-open logging and per-link access counts in the activity log.
Move channel integrations (Instagram, X, LinkedIn) from mock data to real account state.
Signed-in browser QA script covering library, asset page, tasks and activity log.
Write a Codex brief in the repo: mail tables and row level security, Gmail app-password sync and send, review fixes, and a qa/ checklist.
Restore the «تم الرد» external status if the owner wants five statuses.
Later: AI thread summary, extraction of requests and dates, and suggested replies in the mail context panel.
Store mail drafts in the database instead of localStorage so they follow the user across devices.
Add a Vercel cron for mail sync so scheduled outside mail goes out without someone having the page open.
AI thread summary and suggested reply after Version 0.
Optional 'send as me' from each person's own Gmail, alongside the department mailbox
Update the mail artifact to match the build (four external statuses, browser-kept drafts).
Build the messaging tab into the site with Postgres tables and RLS like mail.
Store chat images and files in Google Drive instead of the browser.
Real voice notes via browser microphone and Drive storage.

findings.text: percentUsed has one-decimal resolution and only updates on responses, so measuring cost per ping may be noisy or stale.
With a 5-minute cache, keeping it hot for hours likely costs more than rebuilding it. The mod needs a break-even check.
The 5h limit is account-wide. Several sessions running the mod would each claim the full reserve unless they share one record.
Unverified: whether $.model.fork reads refresh the main thread's 1-hour cache entry. If not, pings waste usage and the cache still expires.
The cost calibration counts other sessions' and subagents' usage, which can inflate the learned rate and over-reserve.
In the desktop app, a held prompt may not be put back into the input box, so the user may have to retype it.
Prototype has no scenario 'today'; dueSoon counts every item due by 23 Sep, so October testers see all work as late.
R01 contains answers in all seven role sections despite single-section branching; authorship of S3-S7 is unconfirmed.
globals.css hard-codes most colours outside six variables, blocking a clean identity switch until tokenised.
Phase 0.2.2 skip directive not yet logged in progress.md, which the project rules require for dated decisions.
Checkpoint 0.3 note still refers to participants testing frozen build 0.2.2.6, now skipped; text is stale.
The design toggle cannot be reached on phone widths or by keyboard, because the logo sits in the sidebar, which is hidden under 700px.
The .claude/ folder, including the new launch.json, is left untracked and uncommitted.
The phone approval sheet only sticks above the bottom bar after scrolling; on first load it partly sits under the navigation bar.
A pre-existing emoji in MVP_draft.md breaks the project's zero-emoji rule; it is still not removed.
Requested calendar moves live in the page's local state and are lost when the user navigates away.
Production alias comms-hub-three.vercel.app is public without authentication; prototype content is visible to anyone with the link.
Prototype state resets on page refresh, so the Director loses test progress if he reloads on Vercel.
ISO dates inside Arabic sentences display reversed (23-09-2026) due to missing direction isolation.
Design switch has no keyboard path; double-click or double-tap only.
Work data is per-browser mock state, so reducer role rules protect interface behaviour only, not shared data; real approval/publish enforcement needs the database.
A reviewer who submitted a work can approve it; nothing prevents self-approval and the spec does not forbid it.
email_status and request_access are callable anonymously, letting anyone test whether an email is an approved account (enumeration).
Legacy qa/*.cjs browser scripts now hit the sign-in gate and cannot run without a signed-in session; qa/auth-gate.cjs has no recorded result.
Supabase Site URL is still http://localhost:3000 with no Redirect URLs, so every confirmation and reset link lands on an unreachable page and masks success or failure.
Resending a confirmation email invalidates the earlier link, which is easy to trip over. The UI now warns about it, but the edit is uncommitted and undeployed.
Supabase Site URL still http://localhost:3000 with empty Redirect URLs, so confirmation and password-reset links land on an unreachable page.
Supabase built-in mailer rate limit blocked resend; each resend also invalidates earlier links, which is easy to trip over during onboarding.
Supabase leaked-password protection is off, and the admin's weak password was shared in chat; the new-password minimum is only 10 characters.
Video playback streams through a serverless function, so long single requests are bounded by the host's function duration limit.
Resume after a dropped connection may restart from byte 0 if the browser cannot read Drive's cross-origin Range header; slower, not incorrect.
Drive upload, resume, CORS and range playback were only tested with a scripted fetch; the first real upload may expose failures.
Supabase leaked-password protection is still off, and a weak admin password was shared in chat and not yet changed.
Google Drive OAuth consent screen cannot be published yet; Drive connection, upload and playback remain unconnected and untested against real Google.
Logo files and Drive code in public/brand and src/lib/drive are uncommitted in the working tree; production deploy is blocked for the agent.
Google OAuth consent screen is still in Testing; Drive refresh tokens expire after 7 days until the app is published.
A logo upload forces Google verification before the OAuth app can be published, blocking the Drive connection.
Supabase leaked-password protection is off and a weak admin password was shared in chat; there is no in-app password change screen.
Privacy and terms pages are static files in public/ that were never fetched locally or on Vercel; their public reachability is unconfirmed.
Google still flags the OAuth app as requiring verification: the homepage domain is unverified and a logo may be present. Publishing worked, but the banner and branding issue persist.
Static privacy.html and terms.html in public/ were never fetched locally or on the deployed site, so their reachability without sign-in is unconfirmed.
Google still flags the OAuth app as requiring verification; the homepage domain is unverified, though Drive upload already works end to end.
The hardcoded mock assets and the new Drive files are separate worlds; nothing links uploads to work items or approvals yet.
Everything is stored in one personal Gmail account on the free 15 GB tier shared with Gmail; capacity and 2-step verification are unconfirmed.
The real media page still uses hardcoded mock assets, separate from the new Drive files. The mock redesign depends on replacing them with real folders and records.
The proposed review-link feature (signed, expiring, no-login links) has no backend design yet. It is shown in the mock but is only a placeholder.
The mock's access model is not tested against the database row level security that would enforce it. Real enforcement of per-folder access is unbuilt.
The real media page still uses hardcoded mock assets, separate from the real Drive files, so pipeline stages and tasks have no backing data.
Media UI and Drive card height fix untested in a real signed-in browser; defects likely surface on first run.
Server-side upload/rename/move/delete route ordering (DB first, then Drive revert) has no automated test; failures could leave Drive and database out of step.
Copy can change on an approved or scheduled asset without returning it to review, so text nobody approved can be published.
The person assigned a task can change its due date, priority and kind without anything being logged.
Direct database inserts into media_files skip the Drive checks in the complete route; an admin can also make another admin through a direct table update.
Approved or scheduled assets can still have their caption changed by view-level roles without returning to review.
Installed Next.js 16.3.5 has critical npm audit advisories (RCE in next/og, SSRF); a fix exists in 16.4.0.
An admin can promote another account to protected admin by direct table update, bypassing add_account's rule.
Without MAIL_SITE_URL, outgoing date-confirmation and review links point to the request origin, possibly localhost, unreachable by outside parties.
Mail approval card counts as waiting while stage is review even if another channel later approves; only patched in the artifact, not the site code.
